method: Offline 240-observation finite stream analysis: largest cross-boundary median shift >1.5 over 13+13 samples estimates step; independent within-regime median pairwise slopes across 10-sample bins, threshold absolute .0027, estimates slow drift even with simultaneous step.

calibration.disclosure: Exploratory; method adjusted using calibration results before freeze.

findings: Distinguishes presence of step and drift across these synthetic conditions in 398/400 cases
Step identified in all 200 step-bearing cases, within ±8 samples
Both failures preserve true step while missing associated slow drift under correlated noise
Zero false event classifications in stable and impulse controls in holdout
limitations: Retrospective/offline algorithm requires full 240 samples; not online detection or zero-latency prediction
Calibration-tuned and condition-aware toy benchmark, not independent external data
One strongest step per stream; no multi-step scenarios
Correlated noise occasionally obscures true drift, as explicitly observed
Not direct evidence of RH or Navier–Stokes claims, physical time dilation, or third-party use of ROOT0 ideas
